title: Adaptive microburst and KV-warmup study for FP8/INT8 quantized variants under long-context and variable batching
creator: Miguel Ortega
description: Goal: Evaluate how FP8 and INT8 quantized kernel selection interacts with dynamic batching and KV-cache warmup behavior for long-context workloads, with special focus on microburst traffic patterns and token-level tail latency. Deliverables: experiment harness, deterministic burst-replay traces, measurement dashboard, recommended KV-warmup and batching heuristics, and a short runbook for production rollout. Scope: 1) Compare FP8 vs INT8 model builds across a spectrum of sequence lengths (1k–65k tokens). 2) Measure latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99/p999) and per-token throughput under three runtime policies: static batching, adaptive microburst batching, and conservative batching with proactive KV warmup. 3) Evaluate quantization-induced accuracy drift on a curated prompt set (QA + code + safety prompts) and flag regressions where output similarity drops below thresholds. 4) Test under varying concurrency patterns (1, 8, 32 sessions) including synthetic microbursts and replayed production sessions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Completed end-to-end runs for FP8 and INT8 variants under all three runtime policies across sequence lengths [1k, 4k, 16k, 32k, 65k]. 2) Dashboard with interactive views for latency percentiles, throughput, and token cost per policy. 3) Evidence (plots + raw CSVs) of microburst-induced tail-latency amplification and mitigations for at least one recommended policy. 4) Accuracy validation report showing edit-distance / embedding-similarity deltas for the prompt set, with a decision matrix (accept/reject/mitigate) per quant/profile. 5) Draft runbook notes for rollout to Dedicated and Hosted with fallback policies.
experiment_plan: Phase A: Build quantized variants (FP8 native, INT8 symmetric) and verify functional parity against FP32 baseline on a small eval set. Phase B: Implement 'burst-replay' harness that replays sampled customer sessions and can inject programmable microbursts (burst size, inter-burst gap). Phase C: Run matrix across batching policies and concurrency levels; collect tokenized latency traces and KV-cache hit/warmup stats. Phase D: Accuracy validation: run curated prompts and collect similarity metrics using embedding cosine and BLEU/EM where appropriate. Phase E: Synthesize findings into recommended runtime heuristics and a small canary rollout plan.
metrics:
- Latency: p50/p90/p95/p99/p999 (ms) per sequence length and policy
- Per-token throughput (tokens/s)
- Cost delta per 1M tokens relative to FP32
- KV-cache warmup time (ms) and warmup hit-rate over first 128 tokens
- Accuracy: embedding cosine delta, token edit-distance, pass-rate on QA correctness checks
- Regression flags: boolean per prompt indicating failure thresholds
bench_config:
- Hardware: A100-40GB and 8xH100 pool (representative of Dedicated)
- Model: open-vendor/7B base -> quantized FP8 and INT8 variants built with runtime-1.22 toolchain
- Batchers: static(batch_size=1/2/4/8), adaptive-microburst (threshold-based queueing with 10ms window), conservative-proactive (pre-warm KV for active sessions)
- Workloads: synthetic bursts (burst sizes 1–128 requests at 100–200 RPS for 10s), replayed traces from sampled prod sessions (anonymized), long-context synthetic sequences (1k to 65k tokens)
- Runs: 10 warmup runs + 25 measurement runs per cell
notes: Initial FP8 kernels reduced p50 by ~8% on 4k sequences but showed a p999 uplift during 32-session microbursts in early runs.
KV-warmup policy that prefetches first 64 token keys reduced tail latency by ~22% for INT8 builds but increased nominal cost by ~3%.

Decision trade-off: proactive KV warmup helps long-lived interactive sessions (sustained context), but harms cost for ephemeral single-shot workloads; propose policy that tags sessions by expected length based on client header.

Accuracy: embedding cosine deltas average 0.02 for FP8 vs FP32 and 0.04 for INT8 on the curated prompt set; QA pass-rate drop of 1.5% for INT8 on code-heavy prompts — requires targeted calibration on final layers.
